01

Section colour crossfade

Scroll. Each section brings its own full-screen colour layer, which fades in when the section's top crosses the middle of the screen.

02

Post it to the back

Every layer is position: fixed at z-index: -1. They stack in document order, so a later section's colour sits over an earlier one, and all of them sit under the content. There's no z-index to juggle.

03

A flag, a query, a fade

A one-step scroll-driven animation flips --in on the section when its top crosses the entry line. The property is registered with inherits: false, so the flip stays on the section.

@container section style(--in: 1) sets the layer's opacity to 1. That comes from the cascade rather than the animation, so an ordinary opacity transition runs, on the compositor.

04
Scrolling decides when. A transition decides how.
05

The nav blends

The nav uses mix-blend-mode against whatever is behind it: color-dodge in dark mode, multiply in light. It follows every fade without knowing which section is showing, and it costs nothing extra while scrolling.

06

The current link

A small IntersectionObserver marks the current link with aria-current. The marker scales up and the label slides over, so both move on the compositor.

07

A short one.

08

No scroll-driven animations?

Then the same observer flips the layers as well, with a data-entered attribute on each section that's past the line. The fade is the same opacity transition.

09

Tune it

Move the entry line with --entry-line on :root. The CSS and the observer both read it. Each section's colour comes from its --hue.

10

That's the lot
